units.label: Browser
units.role: End user submitting the order form.

units.label: Django app
units.role: Django process serving views and dispatching tasks to the Celery broker.

units.label: Redis broker
units.role: Celery broker that queues task messages between Django and the worker pool.

units.label: Celery worker
units.role: Long-running worker process that runs send_receipt, reconcile_inventory, and nightly_purge.

units.label: Postgres
units.role: Primary store for Order, Receipt, StockAdjustment rows.

units.label: SMTP relay
units.role: External mail relay that accepts receipt POSTs.

units.label: Celery beat
units.role: Scheduler process that fires CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE entries on the configured cron expressions.

flows.title: Customer submits the order form
flows.name: Customer submits the order form
flows.tagline: POST /orders → row saved → two tasks queued → 201.
flows.narration: A browser POSTs the order form to Django. The view validates and saves the order row, then queues send_receipt and reconcile_inventory before returning 201.

steps.narration: The order form posts to /orders. The view enforces POST and binds the body to the OrderForm.

steps.payload: INSERT INTO orders_order (...) VALUES (...) RETURNING id
steps.narration: form.save() runs the INSERT against the orders_order table and returns the saved instance.

steps.payload: send_receipt.delay(order.id) → message on the 'celery' default queue.
steps.narration: The view enqueues the receipt task. .delay places a message on Redis tagged for the send_receipt route.

steps.payload: reconcile_inventory.delay(order.id) → message on the 'celery' default queue.
steps.narration: The view enqueues the inventory adjustment task on the same queue. The two messages are independent.
The view returns 201 with the order id. The two tasks are queued but have not run yet.

flows.title: Receipt task runs
flows.name: Receipt task runs
flows.tagline: Worker pops send_receipt → renders → POSTs to SMTP → writes receipt row.
flows.narration: A Celery worker pops send_receipt, loads the order, posts the rendered email to the SMTP relay, and writes a Receipt row. SMTP errors trigger a retry up to three times.

steps.payload: Task envelope for orders.tasks.send_receipt with the order id.
steps.narration: The worker subscribes to the default queue. When a send_receipt message arrives, Celery hands it to the task body.
send_receipt calls Order.objects.get to load the row. The query runs in the worker process's connection.
The task POSTs the rendered HTML to the SMTP relay. A RelayError triggers Celery's retry path.
The relay acknowledges the post with 202; the task proceeds to write the receipt row.

steps.payload: INSERT INTO orders_receipt (order_id, sent_at) VALUES (:oid, now())
steps.narration: Receipt.objects.create writes the audit row, locking in the fact that the email was accepted by the relay.

flows.title: Inventory reconciliation task runs
flows.name: Inventory reconciliation task runs
flows.tagline: Worker pops reconcile_inventory → writes a stock adjustment row.
flows.narration: A Celery worker pops reconcile_inventory, loads the order with its item, and writes a negative stock adjustment row marking the inventory change.

steps.payload: Task envelope for orders.tasks.reconcile_inventory with the order id.
steps.narration: The worker pops the inventory task message from the queue. The body executes in the worker process.

steps.payload: SELECT * FROM orders_order JOIN orders_item ON ... WHERE orders_order.id=:id
steps.narration: Order.objects.select_related('item').get loads the order and its item in a single join.

steps.payload: INSERT INTO orders_stockadjustment (item_id, delta, reason) VALUES (:iid, -:qty, 'order:<id>')
steps.narration: StockAdjustment.objects.create writes the negative delta row. Downstream readers can aggregate adjustments to compute on-hand stock.

flows.title: Celery beat fires the nightly purge
flows.name: Celery beat fires the nightly purge
flows.tagline: Every day at 03:15 → enqueue nightly_purge → worker deletes 90-day-old cancelled orders.
flows.narration: At 03:15 each day Celery beat consults CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE, enqueues nightly_purge on the default queue, and a worker pops it and deletes cancelled orders older than 90 days.

steps.payload: nightly_purge message on the 'celery' default queue.
steps.narration: The beat process compares wall-clock time against each entry. At 03:15 the nightly-purge entry fires and publishes the task message.
A worker subscribed to the default queue pops the message and dispatches the function.

steps.payload: DELETE FROM orders_order WHERE status='cancelled' AND created_at < now() - interval '90 days'
steps.narration: The task computes a cutoff 90 days back and runs the bulk delete. The number of rows removed is logged by Django's ORM.

flows.title: Celery app boots and discovers tasks
flows.name: Celery app boots and discovers tasks
flows.tagline: celery -A orders_project worker → Celery loads settings, autodiscovers, listens.
flows.narration: On worker boot the Celery app loads Django settings under the CELERY_ namespace, autodiscovers tasks in every INSTALLED_APP, and connects to Redis to listen on the default queue.

steps.narration: The Celery app is created and pulls every CELERY_* setting into its config. CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE comes in with it.
Celery scans each installed app for a tasks module and registers every @shared_task it finds.
The worker opens its connection to Redis and subscribes to the default queue. Beat and Django publish into the same queue.

glossary.Celery task: A function decorated with @shared_task that runs out-of-process via a worker.
glossary.Apply async: .delay(...) or .apply_async(...); enqueues a task message on the broker without blocking the caller.
glossary.Retry policy: Celery's built-in retry mechanism configured per task; the example uses max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=30.
glossary.Celery beat: A scheduler that fires task messages on a configured cron schedule.
glossary.Cron expression: A scheduling rule using hour/minute/day-of-week fields; here, hour=3 minute=15 means 03:15 every day.
glossary.Autodiscovery: Celery's mechanism for finding @shared_task definitions across every INSTALLED_APP without explicit imports.
